# ============================================================================
# 1961. Full Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Full Fine-Tuning: Update all model parameters during training.
Use case: When you have sufficient data and computational resources.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from torchvision import models
import copy

class FullFineTuning:
    """
    Complete fine-tuning of all model parameters.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, learning_rate=1e-4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            learning_rate: Learning rate for optimization
        """
        self.model = model
        
        # Replace the final layer for new task
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):  # ResNet-like models
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):  # VGG-like models
            in_features = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            model.classifier[-1] = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        # All parameters are trainable
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = True
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for batch_idx, (data, target) in enumerate(dataloader):
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)


# ============================================================================
# 1962. Feature Extraction Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Feature Extraction: Freeze all layers except the final classifier.
Use case: Small dataset, similar domain to pre-training.
"""

class FeatureExtraction:
    """
    Use pre-trained model as fixed feature extractor.
    Only train the final classification layer.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, learning_rate=1e-3):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            learning_rate: Learning rate for classifier
        """
        self.model = model
        
        # Freeze all layers
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
        
        # Replace and unfreeze final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            trainable_params = model.fc.parameters()
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):
            in_features = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            model.classifier[-1] = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            trainable_params = model.classifier[-1].parameters()
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(trainable_params, lr=learning_rate)
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)


# ============================================================================
# 1963. Layer Freezing Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Layer Freezing: Selectively freeze specific layers.
Use case: Fine-grained control over which layers to update.
"""

class LayerFreezing:
    """
    Freeze specific layers while training others.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, freeze_until_layer=None, learning_rate=1e-4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            freeze_until_layer: Name of layer to freeze up to (exclusive)
            learning_rate: Learning rate
        """
        self.model = model
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        # Freeze layers
        freeze_mode = True
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if freeze_until_layer and freeze_until_layer in name:
                freeze_mode = False
            param.requires_grad = not freeze_mode
        
        # Only optimize trainable parameters
        trainable_params = [p for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(trainable_params, lr=learning_rate)
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def get_trainable_params(self):
        """Return count of trainable parameters"""
        return sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


# ============================================================================
# 1964. Gradual Unfreezing Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Gradual Unfreezing: Progressively unfreeze layers during training.
Use case: Large models, prevent catastrophic forgetting.
"""

class GradualUnfreezing:
    """
    Progressively unfreeze layers from top to bottom.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, learning_rate=1e-4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            learning_rate: Learning rate
        """
        self.model = model
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        # Get all layer names
        self.layer_groups = self._get_layer_groups()
        self.current_group = 0
        
        # Initially freeze all layers
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
        
        # Unfreeze final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            for param in model.fc.parameters():
                param.requires_grad = True
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(
            [p for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad],
            lr=learning_rate
        )
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def _get_layer_groups(self):
        """Group layers for gradual unfreezing"""
        layer_groups = []
        current_group = []
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_children():
            current_group.append(name)
            if len(current_group) >= 2:  # Group every 2 layers
                layer_groups.append(current_group)
                current_group = []
        
        if current_group:
            layer_groups.append(current_group)
        
        return list(reversed(layer_groups))  # Unfreeze from top
    
    def unfreeze_next_layer_group(self):
        """Unfreeze the next group of layers"""
        if self.current_group >= len(self.layer_groups):
            print("All layers already unfrozen")
            return False
        
        group = self.layer_groups[self.current_group]
        for layer_name in group:
            layer = getattr(self.model, layer_name, None)
            if layer is not None:
                for param in layer.parameters():
                    param.requires_grad = True
        
        # Update optimizer with new parameters
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(
            [p for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad],
            lr=self.optimizer.param_groups[0]['lr']
        )
        
        self.current_group += 1
        print(f"Unfroze layer group {self.current_group}: {group}")
        return True
    
    def train_with_unfreezing(self, dataloader, epochs_per_unfreeze=5, device='cuda'):
        """Train with gradual unfreezing"""
        all_losses = []
        
        while True:
            # Train for several epochs
            for epoch in range(epochs_per_unfreeze):
                epoch_loss = self.train_epoch(dataloader, device)
                all_losses.append(epoch_loss)
                print(f"Epoch {len(all_losses)}, Loss: {epoch_loss:.4f}")
            
            # Unfreeze next layer group
            if not self.unfreeze_next_layer_group():
                break
        
        return all_losses
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)


# ============================================================================
# 1965. Discriminative Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Discriminative Fine-Tuning: Different learning rates for different layers.
Use case: Lower layers need smaller updates than higher layers.
"""

class DiscriminativeFinetuning:
    """
    Apply different learning rates to different layers.
    Lower layers get smaller learning rates.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, base_lr=1e-4, lr_multiplier=2.6):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            base_lr: Learning rate for the lowest layer
            lr_multiplier: Multiplier for each subsequent layer group
        """
        self.model = model
        self.base_lr = base_lr
        self.lr_multiplier = lr_multiplier
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        # Create parameter groups with different learning rates
        param_groups = self._create_param_groups()
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(param_groups)
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def _create_param_groups(self):
        """Create parameter groups with discriminative learning rates"""
        # Get all named parameters
        all_params = list(self.model.named_parameters())
        
        # Divide into groups (e.g., by layer depth)
        num_groups = 5
        params_per_group = len(all_params) // num_groups
        
        param_groups = []
        for i in range(num_groups):
            start_idx = i * params_per_group
            end_idx = start_idx + params_per_group if i < num_groups - 1 else len(all_params)
            
            group_params = [p for name, p in all_params[start_idx:end_idx]]
            lr = self.base_lr * (self.lr_multiplier ** i)
            
            param_groups.append({
                'params': group_params,
                'lr': lr
            })
            
            print(f"Group {i}: LR = {lr:.2e}, Params = {len(group_params)}")
        
        return param_groups
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)


# ============================================================================
# 1966. Slanted Triangular Learning Rate Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Slanted Triangular Learning Rate: Gradually increase then decrease LR.
Use case: Fast convergence with stability.
"""

class SlantedTriangularLR:
    """
    Implements slanted triangular learning rate schedule.
    LR increases linearly then decreases linearly.
    """
    def __init__(self, optimizer, num_epochs, num_batches, cut_frac=0.1, 
                 ratio=32, max_lr=1e-3):
        """
        Args:
            optimizer: PyTorch optimizer
            num_epochs: Total number of epochs
            num_batches: Number of batches per epoch
            cut_frac: Fraction of iterations to increase LR
            ratio: Ratio of lowest to highest LR
            max_lr: Maximum learning rate
        """
        self.optimizer = optimizer
        self.num_epochs = num_epochs
        self.num_batches = num_batches
        self.cut_frac = cut_frac
        self.ratio = ratio
        self.max_lr = max_lr
        self.min_lr = max_lr / ratio
        
        self.total_iterations = num_epochs * num_batches
        self.cut = int(self.total_iterations * cut_frac)
        self.current_iter = 0
    
    def step(self):
        """Update learning rate"""
        t = self.current_iter
        
        if t < self.cut:
            # Linear increase
            p = t / self.cut
        else:
            # Linear decrease
            p = 1 - ((t - self.cut) / (self.total_iterations - self.cut))
        
        lr = self.min_lr + p * (self.max_lr - self.min_lr)
        
        for param_group in self.optimizer.param_groups:
            param_group['lr'] = lr
        
        self.current_iter += 1
        return lr
    
    def get_lr(self):
        """Get current learning rate"""
        return self.optimizer.param_groups[0]['lr']


class SlantedTriangularFineTuning:
    """Fine-tuning with slanted triangular learning rate schedule"""
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, num_epochs, num_batches, max_lr=1e-3):
        self.model = model
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.model.parameters())
        self.scheduler = SlantedTriangularLR(
            self.optimizer, num_epochs, num_batches, max_lr=max_lr
        )

# 1967. Warm-Up Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Warm-Up Fine-Tuning: Gradually increase learning rate at the start.
Use case: Prevent early instability in training.
"""

class WarmUpFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tuning with learning rate warm-up.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, warmup_epochs=5, 
                 initial_lr=1e-7, target_lr=1e-4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            warmup_epochs: Number of epochs for warm-up
            initial_lr: Starting learning rate
            target_lr: Target learning rate after warm-up
        """
        self.model = model
        self.warmup_epochs = warmup_epochs
        self.initial_lr = initial_lr
        self.target_lr = target_lr
        self.current_epoch = 0
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=initial_lr)
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def get_warmup_lr(self, epoch):
        """Calculate learning rate for warm-up phase"""
        if epoch < self.warmup_epochs:
            # Linear warm-up
            return self.initial_lr + (self.target_lr - self.initial_lr) * \
                   (epoch / self.warmup_epochs)
        else:
            return self.target_lr
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch with warm-up"""
        # Update learning rate for current epoch
        lr = self.get_warmup_lr(self.current_epoch)
        for param_group in self.optimizer.param_groups:
            param_group['lr'] = lr
        
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        self.current_epoch += 1
        return total_loss / len(dataloader), lr

# 1968. Two-Stage Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Two-Stage Fine-Tuning: Train classifier first, then fine-tune entire model.
Use case: Stabilize classifier before updating backbone.
"""

class TwoStageFineTuning:
    """
    Stage 1: Train only the classifier with frozen backbone.
    Stage 2: Fine-tune the entire model.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, stage1_lr=1e-3, stage2_lr=1e-4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            stage1_lr: Learning rate for stage 1
            stage2_lr: Learning rate for stage 2
        """
        self.model = model
        self.stage1_lr = stage1_lr
        self.stage2_lr = stage2_lr
        self.current_stage = 1
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            self.classifier = model.fc
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):
            in_features = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            model.classifier[-1] = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            self.classifier = model.classifier[-1]
        
        # Stage 1: Freeze backbone
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
        for param in self.classifier.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = True
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.classifier.parameters(), lr=stage1_lr)
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def switch_to_stage2(self):
        """Switch to stage 2: unfreeze all layers"""
        print("Switching to Stage 2: Fine-tuning entire model")
        self.current_stage = 2
        
        # Unfreeze all parameters
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = True
        
        # Create new optimizer for all parameters
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=self.stage2_lr)
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)
    
    def train_two_stage(self, dataloader, stage1_epochs=10, stage2_epochs=20, 
                       device='cuda'):
        """Complete two-stage training"""
        losses = {'stage1': [], 'stage2': []}
        
        # Stage 1
        print(f"Stage 1: Training classifier for {stage1_epochs} epochs")
        for epoch in range(stage1_epochs):
            loss = self.train_epoch(dataloader, device)
            losses['stage1'].append(loss)
            print(f"Stage 1 Epoch {epoch+1}/{stage1_epochs}, Loss: {loss:.4f}")
        
        # Switch to Stage 2
        self.switch_to_stage2()
        
        # Stage 2
        print(f"Stage 2: Fine-tuning entire model for {stage2_epochs} epochs")
        for epoch in range(stage2_epochs):
            loss = self.train_epoch(dataloader, device)
            losses['stage2'].append(loss)
            print(f"Stage 2 Epoch {epoch+1}/{stage2_epochs}, Loss: {loss:.4f}")
        
        return losses


# ============================================================================
# 1969. Multi-Stage Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Multi-Stage Fine-Tuning: Multiple stages with different configurations.
Use case: Complex fine-tuning scenarios requiring multiple phases.
"""

class MultiStageFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tuning with multiple configurable stages.
    Each stage can have different frozen layers and learning rates.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
        """
        self.model = model
        self.stages = []
        self.current_stage_idx = 0
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        self.optimizer = None
    
    def add_stage(self, name, freeze_layers=None, learning_rate=1e-4, 
                  epochs=10, weight_decay=0.0):
        """
        Add a training stage.
        
        Args:
            name: Stage name
            freeze_layers: List of layer names to freeze (None = freeze all except classifier)
            learning_rate: Learning rate for this stage
            epochs: Number of epochs for this stage
            weight_decay: Weight decay for regularization
        """
        stage = {
            'name': name,
            'freeze_layers': freeze_layers,
            'learning_rate': learning_rate,
            'epochs': epochs,
            'weight_decay': weight_decay
        }
        self.stages.append(stage)
        print(f"Added stage: {name} (LR={learning_rate}, Epochs={epochs})")
    
    def _configure_stage(self, stage):
        """Configure model for a specific stage"""
        print(f"\nConfiguring stage: {stage['name']}")
        
        # First, unfreeze all layers
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = True
        
        # Then freeze specified layers
        if stage['freeze_layers'] is not None:
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                for freeze_pattern in stage['freeze_layers']:
                    if freeze_pattern in name:
                        param.requires_grad = False
                        break
        
        # Create optimizer for trainable parameters
        trainable_params = [p for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(
            trainable_params,
            lr=stage['learning_rate'],
            weight_decay=stage['weight_decay']
        )
        
        num_trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in trainable_params)
        print(f"Trainable parameters: {num_trainable:,}")
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
            _, predicted = output.max(1)
            total += target.size(0)
            correct += predicted.eq(target).sum().item()
        
        avg_loss = total_loss / len(dataloader)
        accuracy = 100. * correct / total
        return avg_loss, accuracy
    
    def train_all_stages(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Execute all training stages"""
        all_losses = {}
        
        for stage_idx, stage in enumerate(self.stages):
            print(f"\n{'='*60}")
            print(f"Starting Stage {stage_idx + 1}/{len(self.stages)}: {stage['name']}")
            print(f"{'='*60}")
            
            # Configure this stage
            self._configure_stage(stage)
            
            stage_losses = []
            stage_accuracies = []
            
            # Train for specified epochs
            for epoch in range(stage['epochs']):
                loss, accuracy = self.train_epoch(dataloader, device)
                stage_losses.append(loss)
                stage_accuracies.append(accuracy)
                
                print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{stage['epochs']}: "
                      f"Loss={loss:.4f}, Accuracy={accuracy:.2f}%")
            
            all_losses[stage['name']] = {
                'losses': stage_losses,
                'accuracies': stage_accuracies
            }
        
        return all_losses


# ============================================================================
# 1970. Sequential Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Sequential Fine-Tuning: Fine-tune on multiple datasets sequentially.
Use case: Transfer learning across multiple domains.
"""

class SequentialFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tune on multiple datasets in sequence.
    Useful for continual learning scenarios.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, task_configs):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            task_configs: List of dicts with 'num_classes', 'name', 'lr'
        """
        self.model = model
        self.task_configs = task_configs
        self.task_heads = nn.ModuleDict()
        self.current_task_idx = 0
        
        # Get feature dimension
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.feature_dim = model.fc.in_features
            # Remove original fc layer
            self.model.fc = nn.Identity()
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):
            self.feature_dim = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            self.model.classifier[-1] = nn.Identity()
        
        # Create task-specific heads
        for i, config in enumerate(task_configs):
            task_name = config.get('name', f'task_{i}')
            num_classes = config['num_classes']
            self.task_heads[task_name] = nn.Linear(self.feature_dim, num_classes)
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def set_task(self, task_name, learning_rate=1e-4, freeze_backbone=False):
        """
        Configure model for a specific task.
        
        Args:
            task_name: Name of the task
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            freeze_backbone: Whether to freeze the backbone
        """
        if task_name not in self.task_heads:
            raise ValueError(f"Task {task_name} not found")
        
        self.current_task = task_name
        self.current_head = self.task_heads[task_name]
        
        # Configure parameter freezing
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = not freeze_backbone
        
        # Task head is always trainable
        for param in self.current_head.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = True
        
        # Create optimizer
        if freeze_backbone:
            params = self.current_head.parameters()
        else:
            params = list(self.model.parameters()) + list(self.current_head.parameters())
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(params, lr=learning_rate)
        
        print(f"Configured for task: {task_name}")
        print(f"Backbone frozen: {freeze_backbone}")
    
    def forward(self, x, task_name=None):
        """Forward pass for a specific task"""
        if task_name is None:
            task_name = self.current_task
        
        features = self.model(x)
        output = self.task_heads[task_name](features)
        return output
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch on current task"""
        self.model.train()
        self.current_head.train()
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.forward(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()

loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)
    
    def train_sequential(self, dataloaders, epochs_per_task=10, device='cuda'):
        """
        Train on all tasks sequentially.
        
        Args:
            dataloaders: Dict mapping task names to dataloaders
            epochs_per_task: Number of epochs per task
            device: Device to train on
        """
        results = {}
        
        for task_idx, config in enumerate(self.task_configs):
            task_name = config.get('name', f'task_{task_idx}')
            lr = config.get('lr', 1e-4)
            freeze_backbone = config.get('freeze_backbone', False)
            
            print(f"\n{'='*60}")
            print(f"Training on task: {task_name} ({task_idx + 1}/{len(self.task_configs)})")
            print(f"{'='*60}")
            
            # Configure for this task
            self.set_task(task_name, learning_rate=lr, freeze_backbone=freeze_backbone)
            
            # Train
            task_losses = []
            for epoch in range(epochs_per_task):
                loss = self.train_epoch(dataloaders[task_name], device)
                task_losses.append(loss)
                print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs_per_task}: Loss={loss:.4f}")
            
            results[task_name] = task_losses
        
        return results


# ============================================================================
# 1971. Intermediate Task Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Intermediate Task Fine-Tuning: Fine-tune on intermediate task before target task.
Use case: When intermediate task is more related to target than source.
"""

class IntermediateTaskFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tune on intermediate task(s) before final target task.
    Helps bridge the gap between source and target domains.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, intermediate_classes, target_classes):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            intermediate_classes: Number of classes for intermediate task
            target_classes: Number of classes for target task
        """
        self.model = model
        self.intermediate_classes = intermediate_classes
        self.target_classes = target_classes
        
        # Get feature dimension
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.feature_dim = model.fc.in_features
            self.model.fc = nn.Identity()
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):
            self.feature_dim = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            self.model.classifier[-1] = nn.Identity()
        
        # Create heads for both tasks
        self.intermediate_head = nn.Linear(self.feature_dim, intermediate_classes)
        self.target_head = nn.Linear(self.feature_dim, target_classes)
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        self.current_phase = 'intermediate'
    
    def configure_intermediate_phase(self, learning_rate=1e-4):
        """Configure for intermediate task training"""
        print("Configuring for intermediate task")
        self.current_phase = 'intermediate'
        
        # All parameters trainable
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = True
        
        params = list(self.model.parameters()) + list(self.intermediate_head.parameters())
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(params, lr=learning_rate)
    
    def configure_target_phase(self, learning_rate=1e-4, freeze_backbone=False):
        """Configure for target task training"""
        print("Configuring for target task")
        self.current_phase = 'target'
        
        # Configure freezing
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = not freeze_backbone
        
        if freeze_backbone:
            params = self.target_head.parameters()
        else:
            params = list(self.model.parameters()) + list(self.target_head.parameters())
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(params, lr=learning_rate)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        """Forward pass through current head"""
        features = self.model(x)
        if self.current_phase == 'intermediate':
            return self.intermediate_head(features)
        else:
            return self.target_head(features)
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        if self.current_phase == 'intermediate':
            self.intermediate_head.train()
        else:
            self.target_head.train()
        
        total_loss = 0
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.forward(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
            _, predicted = output.max(1)
            total += target.size(0)
            correct += predicted.eq(target).sum().item()
        
        avg_loss = total_loss / len(dataloader)
        accuracy = 100. * correct / total
        return avg_loss, accuracy
    
    def train_with_intermediate(self, intermediate_dataloader, target_dataloader,
                               intermediate_epochs=20, target_epochs=30,
                               intermediate_lr=1e-4, target_lr=1e-5,
                               freeze_for_target=False, device='cuda'):
        """
        Complete training pipeline with intermediate task.
        
        Args:
            intermediate_dataloader: DataLoader for intermediate task
            target_dataloader: DataLoader for target task
            intermediate_epochs: Epochs for intermediate task
            target_epochs: Epochs for target task
            intermediate_lr: Learning rate for intermediate task
            target_lr: Learning rate for target task
            freeze_for_target: Whether to freeze backbone for target task
            device: Device to train on
        """
        results = {'intermediate': [], 'target': []}
        
        # Phase 1: Intermediate task
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("Phase 1: Training on Intermediate Task")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        self.configure_intermediate_phase(learning_rate=intermediate_lr)
        
        for epoch in range(intermediate_epochs):
            loss, acc = self.train_epoch(intermediate_dataloader, device)
            results['intermediate'].append({'loss': loss, 'accuracy': acc})
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{intermediate_epochs}: Loss={loss:.4f}, Acc={acc:.2f}%")
        
        # Phase 2: Target task
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("Phase 2: Training on Target Task")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        self.configure_target_phase(learning_rate=target_lr, 
                                    freeze_backbone=freeze_for_target)
        
        for epoch in range(target_epochs):
            loss, acc = self.train_epoch(target_dataloader, device)
            results['target'].append({'loss': loss, 'accuracy': acc})
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{target_epochs}: Loss={loss:.4f}, Acc={acc:.2f}%")
        
        return results


# ============================================================================
# 1972. Auxiliary Task Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Auxiliary Task Fine-Tuning: Train on main task with auxiliary tasks simultaneously.
Use case: Improve generalization through multi-task learning.
"""

class AuxiliaryTaskFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tune with auxiliary tasks to improve main task performance.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, main_classes, auxiliary_tasks):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            main_classes: Number of classes for main task
            auxiliary_tasks: List of dicts with 'name', 'num_classes', 'weight'
        """
        self.model = model
        self.auxiliary_tasks = auxiliary_tasks
        
        # Get feature dimension
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.feature_dim = model.fc.in_features
            self.model.fc = nn.Identity()
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):
            self.feature_dim = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            self.model.classifier[-1] = nn.Identity()
        
        # Create main task head
        self.main_head = nn.Linear(self.feature_dim, main_classes)
        
        # Create auxiliary task heads
        self.aux_heads = nn.ModuleDict()
        for task in auxiliary_tasks:
            self.aux_heads[task['name']] = nn.Linear(
                self.feature_dim, task['num_classes']
            )
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def forward(self, x):
        """Forward pass through all heads"""
        features = self.model(x)
        
        outputs = {
            'main': self.main_head(features)
        }
        
        for task_name, head in self.aux_heads.items():
            outputs[task_name] = head(features)
        
        return outputs
    
    def compute_loss(self, outputs, targets):
        """
        Compute weighted loss from main and auxiliary tasks.
        
        Args:
            outputs: Dict of outputs from forward pass
            targets: Dict of targets for each task
        """
        # Main task loss
        main_loss = self.criterion(outputs['main'], targets['main'])
        total_loss = main_loss
        
        # Auxiliary task losses
        aux_losses = {}
        for task in self.auxiliary_tasks:
            task_name = task['name']
            if task_name in targets:
                aux_loss = self.criterion(outputs[task_name], targets[task_name])
                aux_losses[task_name] = aux_loss
                total_loss += task['weight'] * aux_loss
        
        return total_loss, main_loss, aux_losses
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """
        Train for one epoch with auxiliary tasks.
        
        Args:
            dataloader: Should yield (data, targets_dict) where targets_dict
                       contains 'main' and auxiliary task labels
        """
        self.model.train()
        self.main_head.train()
        for head in self.aux_heads.values():
            head.train()
        
        total_loss = 0
        main_loss_sum = 0
        aux_loss_sums = {task['name']: 0 for task in self.auxiliary_tasks}
        
        for data, targets in dataloader:
            # Move data to device
            data = data.to(device)
            targets = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in targets.items()}
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = self.forward(data)
            loss, main_loss, aux_losses = self.compute_loss(outputs, targets)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
            main_loss_sum += main_loss.item()
            for task_name, aux_loss in aux_losses.items():
                aux_loss_sums[task_name] += aux_loss.item()
        
        n_batches = len(dataloader)
        results = {
            'total_loss': total_loss / n_batches,
            'main_loss': main_loss_sum / n_batches,
            'aux_losses': {k: v / n_batches for k, v in aux_loss_sums.items()}
        }
        
        return results
    
    def configure_optimizer(self, learning_rate=1e-4):
        """Configure optimizer for all parameters"""
        params = list(self.model.parameters()) + \
                list(self.main_head.parameters())
        
        for head in self.aux_heads.values():
            params += list(head.parameters())
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(params, lr=learning_rate)

# 1973. Multi-Task Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Multi-Task Fine-Tuning: Train on multiple tasks simultaneously with equal importance.
Use case: When multiple target tasks are equally important.
"""

class MultiTaskFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tune on multiple tasks simultaneously.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, task_configs):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            task_configs: List of dicts with 'name', 'num_classes', 'weight'
        """
        self.model = model
        self.task_configs = task_configs
        
        # Get feature dimension
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.feature_dim = model.fc.in_features
            self.model.fc = nn.Identity()
        elif hasattr(model, 'classifier'):
            self.feature_dim = model.classifier[-1].in_features
            self.model.classifier[-1] = nn.Identity()
        
        # Create task-specific heads
        self.task_heads = nn.ModuleDict()
        for task in task_configs:
            self.task_heads[task['name']] = nn.Linear(
                self.feature_dim, task['num_classes']
            )
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    def forward(self, x, task_names=None):
        """
        Forward pass through specified task heads.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            task_names: List of task names (None = all tasks)
        """
        features = self.model(x)
        
        if task_names is None:
            task_names = list(self.task_heads.keys())
        
        outputs = {}
        for task_name in task_names:
            outputs[task_name] = self.task_heads[task_name](features)
        
        return outputs
    
    def compute_multi_task_loss(self, outputs, targets):
        """
        Compute weighted multi-task loss.
        
        Args:
            outputs: Dict of task outputs
            targets: Dict of task targets
        """
        total_loss = 0
        task_losses = {}
        
        for task in self.task_configs:
            task_name = task['name']
            if task_name in outputs and task_name in targets:
                loss = self.criterion(outputs[task_name], targets[task_name])
                task_losses[task_name] = loss
                weight = task.get('weight', 1.0)
                total_loss += weight * loss
        
        return total_loss, task_losses
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """
        Train for one epoch on multiple tasks.
        
        Args:
            dataloader: Should yield (data, targets_dict) where targets_dict
                       maps task names to their targets
        """
        self.model.train()
        for head in self.task_heads.values():

        total_loss_sum = 0
        task_loss_sums = {task['name']: 0 for task in self.task_configs}
        task_correct = {task['name']: 0 for task in self.task_configs}
        task_total = {task['name']: 0 for task in self.task_configs}
        
        for data, targets in dataloader:
            data = data.to(device)
            targets = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in targets.items()}
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = self.forward(data)
            total_loss, task_losses =

            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss_sum += total_loss.item()
            
            # Track per-task metrics
            for task_name, loss in task_losses.items():
                task_loss_sums[task_name] += loss.item()
                
                # Calculate accuracy
                _, predicted = outputs[task_name].max(1)
                task_total[task_name] += targets[task_name].size(0)
                task_correct[task_name] += predicted.eq(targets[task_name]).sum().item()
        
        n_batches = len(dataloader)
        results = {
            'total_loss': total_loss_sum / n_batches,
            'task_metrics': {}
        }
        
        for task_name in task_loss_sums.keys():
            results['task_metrics'][task_name] = {
                'loss': task_loss_sums[task_name] / n_batches,
                'accuracy': 100. * task_correct[task_name] / task_total[task_name]
            }
        
        return results
    
    def configure_optimizer(self, learning_rate=1e-4, weight_decay=0.0):
        """Configure optimizer for all parameters"""
        params = list(self.model.parameters())
        for head in self.task_heads.values():
            params += list(head.parameters())
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(params, lr=learning_rate, weight_decay=weight_decay)


# ============================================================================
# 1974. Continual Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Continual Fine-Tuning: Fine-tune on sequence of tasks while preventing forgetting.
Use case: Lifelong learning scenarios.
"""

class ContinualFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tune on tasks sequentially while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
    Uses Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) approach.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, ewc_lambda=0.4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of classes (can be updated per task)
            ewc_lambda: Importance of previous task parameters
        """
        self.model = model
        self.ewc_lambda = ewc_lambda
        
        # Store Fisher information and optimal parameters
        self.fisher_dict = {}
        self.optpar_dict = {}
        
        # Replace final layer
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.feature_dim = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(self.feature_dim, num_classes)
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        self.current_task = 0
    
    def compute_fisher_matrix(self, dataloader, device='cuda', sample_size=200):
        """
        Compute Fisher Information Matrix for current task.
        
        Args:
            dataloader: DataLoader for current task
            device: Device to compute on
            sample_size: Number of samples to use
        """
        print("Computing Fisher Information Matrix...")
        self.model.eval()
        
        # Initialize Fisher information
        fisher = {n: torch.zeros_like(p) for n, p in self.model.named_parameters() 
                  if p.requires_grad}
        
        # Sample from dataloader
        samples_seen = 0
        for data, target in dataloader:
            if samples_seen >= sample_size:
                break
            
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            # Forward pass
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            
            # Backward pass
            self.model.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            
            # Accumulate squared gradients
            for n, p in self.model.named_parameters():
                if p.requires_grad and p.grad is not None:
                    fisher[n] += p.grad.data ** 2
            
            samples_seen += data.size(0)
        
        # Normalize by number of samples
        for n in fisher.keys():
            fisher[n] /= samples_seen
        
        return fisher
    
    def ewc_loss(self):
        """Compute EWC regularization loss"""
        if not self.fisher_dict:
            return 0
        
        loss = 0
        for task_id, fisher in self.fisher_dict.items():
            for n, p in self.model.named_parameters():
                if n in fisher:
                    loss += (fisher[n] * (p - self.optpar_dict[task_id][n]) ** 2).sum()
        
        return self.ewc_lambda * loss
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch with EWC regularization"""
        self.model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        total_task_loss = 0
        total_ewc_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Task loss
            output = self.model(data)
            task_loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            
            # EWC loss
            ewc_loss = self.ewc_loss()
            
            # Total loss
            loss = task_loss + ewc_loss
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
            total_task_loss += task_loss.item()
            total_ewc_loss += ewc_loss if isinstance(ewc_loss, float) else ewc_loss.item()
        
        n_batches = len(dataloader)
        return {
            'total_loss': total_loss / n_batches,
            'task_loss': total_task_loss / n_batches,
            'ewc_loss': total_ewc_loss / n_batches
        }
    
    def train_new_task(self, dataloader, task_id, epochs=10, learning_rate=1e-4, 
                       device='cuda'):
        """
        Train on a new task.
        
        Args:
            dataloader: DataLoader for new task
            task_id: Identifier for this task
            epochs: Number of training epochs
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            device: Device to train on
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"Training on Task {task_id}")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Configure optimizer
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        
        # Train
        for epoch in range(epochs):
            losses = self.train_epoch(dataloader, device)
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs}: "
                  f"Total Loss={losses['total_loss']:.4f}, "
                  f"Task Loss={losses['task_loss']:.4f}, "
                  f"EWC Loss={losses['ewc_loss']:.4f}")
        
        # After training, compute Fisher information
        fisher = self.compute_fisher_matrix(dataloader, device)
        self.fisher_dict[task_id] = fisher
        
        # Store optimal parameters
        self.optpar_dict[task_id] = {
            n: p.data.clone() for n, p in self.model.named_parameters() 
            if p.requires_grad
        }
        
        self.current_task = task_id
        print(f"Task {task_id} training complete. Fisher matrix stored.")


# ============================================================================
# 1975. Adapter-Based Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Adapter-Based Fine-Tuning: Insert small adapter modules between layers.
Use case: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning, multiple tasks.
"""

class AdapterModule(nn.Module):
    """
    Adapter module to insert between transformer layers.
    """
    def __init__(self, input_dim, bottleneck_dim=64):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input/output dimension
            bottleneck_dim: Bottleneck dimension (smaller = more efficient)
        """
        super(AdapterModule, self).__init__()
        
        self.down_project = nn.Linear(input_dim, bottleneck_dim)
        self.activation = nn.ReLU()
        self.up_project = nn.Linear(bottleneck_dim, input_dim)
        
        # Initialize with small weights
        nn.init.normal_(self.down_project.weight, std=1e-3)
        nn.init.normal_(self.up_project.weight, std=1e-3)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.down_project.bias)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.up_project.bias)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        """Forward pass with residual connection"""
        residual = x
        x = self.down_project(x)
        x = self.activation(x)
        x = self.up_project(x)
        return x + residual  # Residual connection


class AdapterFineTuning:
    """
    Fine-tuning using adapter modules.
    Only adapter parameters are trained.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, adapter_dim=64, adapter_positions=None):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            adapter_dim: Bottleneck dimension for adapters
            adapter_positions: List of layer names to add adapters after
        """
        self.model = model
        self.adapters = nn.ModuleDict()
        
        # Freeze all original parameters
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
        
        # Add adapters to specified positions
        if adapter_positions is None:
            # Default: add adapter after each major block
            adapter_positions = self._get_default_positions()
        
        # Insert adapters
        for pos_name in adapter_positions:
            # Get the dimension at this position
            dim = self._get_layer_dim(pos_name)
            if dim is not None:
                self.adapters[pos_name] = AdapterModule(dim, adapter_dim)
        
        # Replace final classifier
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            # Make classifier trainable
            for param in model.fc.parameters():
                param.requires_grad = True
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        # Configure optimizer for adapters and classifier only
        adapter_params = []
        for adapter in self.adapters.values():
            adapter_params += list(adapter.parameters())
        
        classifier_params = list(model.fc.parameters()) if hasattr(model, 'fc') else []
        
        self.trainable_params = adapter_params + classifier_params
        print(f"Total trainable parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in self.trainable_params):,}")
    
    def _get_default_positions(self):
        """Get default positions to insert adapters"""
        positions = []
        for name, module in self.model.named_children():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Sequential):
                positions.append(name)
        return positions
    
    def _get_layer_dim(self, layer_name):
        """Get output dimension of a layer"""
        try:
            layer = dict(self.model.named_modules())[layer_name]
            if hasattr(layer, 'out_features'):
                return layer.out_features
            elif hasattr(layer, 'num_features'):
                return layer.num_features
        except:
            pass
        return None
    
    def forward_with_adapters(self, x):
        """
        Forward pass with adapter injection.
        Note: This is a simplified version. Real implementation would need
        to hook into the model's forward pass.
        """
        # This is model-specific and would need customization
        output = self.model(x)
        return output
    
    def configure_optimizer(self, learning_rate=1e-3):
        """Configure optimizer for trainable parameters only"""
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.trainable_params, lr=learning_rate)
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        for adapter in self.adapters.values():
            adapter.train()
        
        total_loss = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
        
        return total_loss / len(dataloader)


# ============================================================================
# 1976. LoRA Fine-Tuning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation): Add low-rank decomposition matrices to weights.
Use case: Extremely parameter-efficient fine-tuning for large models.
"""

class LoRALayer(nn.Module):
    """
    LoRA layer that adds low-rank adaptation to existing linear layer.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, rank=4, alpha=1):
        """
        Args:
            in_features: Input dimension
            out_features: Output dimension
            rank: Rank of the low-rank matrices
            alpha: Scaling factor
        """
        super(LoRALayer, self).__init__()
        
        self.rank = rank
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.scaling = alpha / rank
        
        # Low-rank matrices
        self.lora_A = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(in_features, rank))
        self.lora_B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(rank, out_features))
        
        # Initialize
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.lora_A, a=5**0.5)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.lora_B)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        """Compute low-rank adaptation"""
        # x @ A @ B
        return (x @ self.lora_A @ self.lora_B) * self.scaling


class LoRAFineTuning:
    """
    LoRA-based fine-tuning.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, rank=4, alpha=1, target_modules=None):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            rank: Rank for LoRA matrices
            alpha: Scaling factor
            target_modules: List of module names to apply LoRA to
        """
        self.model = model
        self.rank = rank
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.lora_layers = nn.ModuleDict()
        
        # Freeze all original parameters
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
        
        # Add LoRA to target modules
        if target_modules is None:
            target_modules = self._get_linear_layers()
        
        for module_name in target_modules:
            module = self._get_module_by_name(module_name)
            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                # Create LoRA layer
                lora = LoRALayer(
                    module.in_features,
                    module.out_features,
                    rank=rank,
                    alpha=alpha
                )
                self.lora_layers[module_name] = l
```python
ora
                
                # Register forward hook to add LoRA output
                self._register_lora_hook(module, lora)
        
        # Replace final classifier
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            for param in model.fc.parameters():
                param.requires_grad = True
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        # Collect trainable parameters
        self.trainable_params = []
        for lora in self.lora_layers.values():
            self.trainable_params += list(lora.parameters())
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.trainable_params += list(model.fc.parameters())
        
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.trainable_params)
        print(f"LoRA trainable parameters: {total_params:,}")
    
    def _get_linear_layers(self):
        """Get names of all linear layers"""
        linear_layers = []
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear) and 'fc' not in name:
                linear_layers.append(name)
        return linear_layers
    
    def _get_module_by_name(self, name):
        """Get module by its name"""
        module = self.model
        for attr in name.split('.'):
            module = getattr(module, attr)
        return module
    
    def _register_lora_hook(self, module, lora_layer):
        """Register forward hook to add LoRA adaptation"""
        def hook(module, input, output):
            # Add LoRA output to original output
            lora_output = lora_layer(input[0])
            return output + lora_output
        
        module.register_forward_hook(hook)
    
    def configure_optimizer(self, learning_rate=1e-3):
        """Configure optimizer for LoRA parameters only"""
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.trainable_params, lr=learning_rate)
    
    def train_epoch(self, dataloader, device='cuda'):
        """Train for one epoch"""
        self.model.train()
        for lora in self.lora_layers.values():
            lora.train()
        
        total_loss = 0
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        
        for data, target in dataloader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            
            self.optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(data)
            loss = self.criterion(output, target)
            loss.backward()
            self.optimizer.step()
            
            total_loss += loss.item()
            _, predicted = output.max(1)
            total += target.size(0)
            correct += predicted.eq(target).sum().item()
        
        avg_loss = total_loss / len(dataloader)
        accuracy = 100. * correct / total
        return avg_loss, accuracy
    
    def merge_lora_weights(self):
        """Merge LoRA weights into original model (for inference)"""
        print("Merging LoRA weights into base model...")
        with torch.no_grad():
            for module_name, lora in self.lora_layers.items():
                module = self._get_module_by_name(module_name)
                if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                    # Compute LoRA weight: W + alpha/r * A @ B
                    lora_weight = lora.lora_A @ lora.lora_B * lora.scaling
                    module.weight.data += lora_weight.T

"""
QLoRA: Quantized LoRA for even more efficient fine-tuning.
Use case: Fine-tune very large models on limited hardware.
"""

class QLoRAFineTuning:
    """
    QLoRA: Combines 4-bit quantization with LoRA.
    Note: Requires bitsandbytes library for full implementation.
    This is a simplified version showing the concept.
    """
    def __init__(self, model, num_classes, rank=4, alpha=1,

            model: Pre-trained model
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            rank: Rank for LoRA matrices
            alpha: Scaling factor
            quantize_base: Whether to quantize base model weights
            target_modules: List of module names to apply LoRA to
        """
        self.model = model
        self.rank = rank
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.lora_layers = nn.ModuleDict()
        
        # Freeze and optionally quantize base model
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
            if quantize_base:
                # In practice, use bitsandbytes for proper 4-bit quantization
                # This is a placeholder showing the concept
                param.data = self._quantize_to_4bit(param.data)
        
        # Add LoRA layers (same as regular LoRA)
        if target_modules is None:
            target_modules = self._get_linear_layers()
        
        for module_name in target_modules:
            module = self._get_module_by_name(module_name)
            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                lora = LoRALayer(
                    module.in_features,
                    module.out_features,
                    rank=rank,
                    alpha=alpha
                )
                self.lora_layers[module_name] = lora
                self._register_lora_hook(module, lora)
        
        # Replace classifier
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            in_features = model.fc.in_features
            model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
            for param in model.fc.parameters():
                param.requires_grad = True
        
        self.criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        # Collect trainable parameters (only LoRA and classifier)
        self.trainable_params = []
        for lora in self.lora_layers.values():
            self.trainable_params += list(lora.parameters())
        if hasattr(model, 'fc'):
            self.trainable_params += list(model.fc.parameters())
        
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.trainable_params)
        total_model_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters())
        print(f"QLoRA trainable parameters: {total_params:,}")
        print(f"Percentage of total: {100 * total_params / total_model_params:.2f}%")
    
    def _quantize_to_4bit(self, tensor):
